authorized_evidence.content:
Onboarding Basics

New employees complete onboarding during their first 10 business days. Required onboarding includes security training, benefits enrollment, department orientation, and access review. Managers are responsible for assigning a buddy and scheduling the first 30-day check-in.

Employees should complete mandatory security awareness training before accessing customer data or production systems.

Personal Devices

Personal devices may be used for limited work access only when enrolled in approved mobile device management or when access occurs through approved browser-based tools. Personal devices must use a passcode, supported operating system, and automatic lock.

Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should be accessed only through approved company systems.

Storage Rules

Internal, Confidential, and Restricted data must be stored in approved company systems. Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should not be stored in local folders unless there is a documented business need.

Company Devices

Employees who regularly access company systems should use a company-managed device. Company devices must have disk encryption, endpoint protection, automatic screen lock, and current operating system updates.

Employees may not disable security tools or remove device management controls from company devices.

Local Storage

Customer data, restricted data, and regulated data should not be stored locally unless there is a documented business need and approved protection. Files should be stored in company-approved cloud storage with access controls.

Sharing Rules

Employees may share data only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Confidential and Restricted data must not be shared in public channels or with unapproved external recipients.

Sales materials may be shared externally only when marked as customer-approved or public-facing.

Security Expectations

Remote work must follow the Device and BYOD Security Policy and the Data Classification and Handling Policy. Confidential and restricted data may only be accessed on approved devices using company-approved tools.

Related Policies

Device requirements are defined in the Device and BYOD Security Policy. Data handling requirements are defined in the Data Classification and Handling Policy.

Approved Software

Employees should use company-approved software for messaging, file storage, source control, project tracking, and customer collaboration. Unapproved software that stores company data must not be used without IT review.

Classification Levels

Northstar uses four data classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted.

Public data is approved for external sharing. Internal data is intended for Northstar employees. Confidential data includes customer business information, financial forecasts, non-public sales materials, and employee operational data. Restricted data includes secrets, credentials, regulated customer data, privileged security records, and sensitive HR case material.
